Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank data (compiled from ITU) show 13.18% of Chad's population using the internet in 2023, and the ITU Digital Development Dashboard gives an ITU estimate of 12% for 2022. Both figures sit within the <15% band. Score of 1 upheld.
revised_comments: An estimated 13% of Chad's population used the internet in 2023, according to World Bank data compiled from ITU sources, placing internet usage in the lowest adoption band on this scale.

Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
revision_notes: The original score relied on a 2015-16 fixed-broadband-only bandwidth estimate (0.73 kbit/s per user) sourced from an old World Bank/ITU series which has since lapsed for Chad. The current ITU Digital Development Dashboard for Chad (published February 2024, data collected to December 2023) reports international bandwidth per Internet user of 21 kbit/s for 2022, placing Chad in the Moderate (20-49 kbit/s) band rather than Very Low. Score revised to 3.
revised_comments: Chad's international internet bandwidth stood at approximately 21 kbit/s per internet user in 2022, according to the ITU Digital Development Dashboard, placing the country in the moderate band for international connectivity capacity.

Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank SDG7 tracking data (as reported via Macrotrends and Trading Economics, both citing the World Bank WDI series) show electricity access in Chad at 12.0% of population in 2023, matching the original comment. Falls within the <25% band. Score of 1 upheld. A direct fetch of the World Bank indicator page returned malformed content, so the figure was corroborated via two independent aggregators of the same underlying WDI series.
revised_comments: Around 12% of Chad's population had access to electricity in 2023, according to World Bank data, among the lowest electrification rates in the world.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Value Name: Severe (frequent daily outages or regular load shedding)
revision_notes: The original score cited a generic Enterprise Surveys link and a '96% outages' figure that could not be traced to a specific published data point; no 2023 Enterprise Survey exists for Chad. The most recent World Bank Enterprise Survey for Chad (2018, the last one conducted) reports that 70.2% of firms experienced electrical outages, with an average of 4.5 outages per typical month — roughly weekly. This corresponds to the 'Poor (weekly outages, intermittent load shedding)' band rather than 'Severe'. Score revised to 2. This remains the most recent authoritative figure since no newer Enterprise Survey round has been fielded in Chad.
revised_comments: Firms in Chad experience frequent power disruptions: the World Bank Enterprise Survey (the most recent round, 2018) records an average of 4.5 outages per month and 70% of firms affected, reflecting poor grid reliability.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank data (compiled from IEA statistics) show renewable electricity output in Chad at 4.61% of total generation in 2021, the most recent year available in this series, consistent with the original comment of approximately 5% for 2022. Falls within the <10% band. Score of 1 upheld.
revised_comments: Renewables contributed around 5% of Chad's electricity generation as of the most recent World Bank/IEA data, with the great majority of generation coming from oil-fired thermal plants.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: The original score of 1 (Gap >60pp) was not calculated from disaggregated urban/rural figures. World Bank SDG7 tracking data for 2023 show urban electricity access in Chad at 48.1% and rural access at 0.4%, a gap of 47.7 percentage points, which falls within the 41-60pp band rather than >60pp. Score revised to 2.
revised_comments: Electricity access in Chad is heavily concentrated in urban areas: World Bank data for 2023 show 48% of the urban population with access to electricity compared with under 1% of the rural population, a gap of roughly 48 percentage points.
